name: AT86RF233-ZU
title: Low-power 2.4 GHz IEEE 802.15.4 transceiver for ZigBee, RF4CE and 6LoWPAN
summary: A single-chip 2.4 GHz radio for IEEE 802.15.4 networks (ZigBee, RF4CE, 6LoWPAN) and other ISM-band links. It needs only an antenna path, a 16 MHz crystal and bypass capacitors around it, and a host talks to it over an SPI slave plus IRQ, SLP_TR and /RST lines. On chip are the O-QPSK modem, a 128-byte frame buffer, two 1.8 V regulators, a hardware MAC (automatic acknowledge, CSMA-CA and retries, address filter, FCS), a 128-bit AES engine and a true random number generator. Sensitivity is -101 dBm at 250 kb/s, output power runs from -17 dBm to +4 dBm, and data rates of 500, 1000 and 2000 kb/s are available beyond the standard. It runs from 1.8 V to 3.6 V in a 5 mm x 5 mm 32-pin QFN; the -ZU parts cover -40 °C to +85 °C and the -ZF parts -40 °C to +125 °C.

circuits.title: Basic application circuit
circuits.description: The smallest working radio: a 50 Ω single-ended RF connector goes through balun B1 to the 100 Ω differential port, with C1 and C2 blocking DC on each side and C4 an optional matching shunt on the 50 Ω side. VDD feeds EVDD and DEVDD, each decoupled by 1 µF (CB2, CB4); CB1 and CB3, 100 nF each, steady the internal AVDD and DVDD regulators. The 16 MHz crystal sits between XTAL1 and XTAL2 with 12 pF from each pin to ground. R1 and C3 form a low-pass on CLKM, sized for 1 MHz, so its harmonics stay off the RF and crystal pins; they are left out when CLKM is not used. DIG1 to DIG4 are tied to ground, and the SPI, IRQ, SLP_TR and /RST lines run to the host.

notes: Place every bypass capacitor right at its pin with a short, low-inductance ground return.
Keep the crystal traces short, low in stray capacitance and away from digital lines; this matters most in the high data rate modes.
Split the board ground into analog, digital, antenna and crystal areas joined at the exposed pad.
When CLKM is not used it is switched off during initialisation and R1, C3 are not fitted.

circuits.title: Extended feature application circuit
circuits.description: The same chip set up for antenna diversity and an external front end. The balun B1 joins RFP/RFN to RF switch SW1, which picks between the receive path through the optional LNA N2 and the transmit path through the external PA N1. A second switch SW2 connects those paths to antenna ANT0 or ANT1. DIG3 and its complement DIG4 (the RX/TX indicator) set SW1, SW2 and the enables of N1 and N2; DIG1 tells SW2 which antenna to use, chosen by the on-chip diversity search while receiving. DIG2 carries the RX and TX frame time stamp to the host. Supply, regulator bypass, crystal and CLKM filter parts sit as in the basic circuit.

operation.text: The receive chain is LNA, polyphase filter, channel band-pass, limiter and ADC into a digital demodulator; the limiter also gives the RSSI. The transmitter modulates the fractional-N PLL directly with O-QPSK, half-sine shaped, 32-chip spreading, and drives the PA. Receiver and PA share the RFP/RFN pins, so no TX/RX switch is needed for a single antenna.

The port expects a 100 Ω differential load. RFP and RFN may be joined at DC, but neither may have a DC path to ground or supply. The pins sit at 0.9 V common mode while transmitting (set by a feedback loop, so each pin may see under 30 pF to ground), at about 20 mV in receive, and are grounded in TRX_OFF to keep them under 1.8 V.

EVDD feeds the analog regulator AVREG and DEVDD the digital regulator DVREG; both make 1.8 V from a 1.25 V bandgap and need bypass capacitors at AVDD and DVDD, whose size sets their settling time. A low-power regulator holds DVDD near 1.5 V in sleep so registers are kept; its bias adds about 100 nA. Setting AVREG_EXT and DVREG_EXT in VREG_CTRL lets an external regulated 1.8 V feed pins 13, 14 and 29, but VDD must still be connected. AVDD_OK and DVDD_OK report a settled supply.

When VDD first appears the chip resets itself, starts the crystal and puts out 1 MHz on CLKM once the oscillator is stable (about 330 µs). The SPI and DVREG are on and the digital inputs have pulls. Before leaving P_ON the host holds SLP_TR low, /RST high and /SEL high, enables IRQ_4 (AWAKE_END) and writes TRX_OFF to TRX_CMD; IRQ_4 marks arrival in TRX_OFF. A /RST pulse is optional but helps the host and radio start in step.

States change by writing TRX_CMD (register 0x02) or by the SLP_TR and /RST pins, and every change is confirmed by reading TRX_STATUS; while it shows 0x1F no further change may be requested. FORCE_TRX_OFF cuts off any receive or transmit at once, whereas TRX_OFF waits for it to finish. FORCE_PLL_ON jumps to PLL_ON from any awake state without turning off the PLL or AVREG. SLP_TR should be low before the force commands are used.

TRX_OFF keeps the crystal, SPI and DVREG running so registers, buffer and AES stay reachable, with the analog front end off. PLL_ON starts AVREG, then locks the PLL to the selected channel and flags IRQ_0; it is the 802.15.4 TX_ON state. RX_ON listens; a valid SHR moves the chip to BUSY_RX and a valid PHR raises IRQ_2, and the frame end raises IRQ_3.

From TRX_OFF, SLP_TR high puts the radio to sleep; only the SLP_TR and /RST monitors stay alive. If CLKM runs above 250 kHz it gives 35 more cycles first so a clocked host can finish; at 250 kHz or 62.5 kHz it stops at once. Registers and AES keys survive, the frame buffer does not. SLP_TR low wakes it to TRX_OFF in about 210 µs; /RST low in SLEEP also returns to TRX_OFF but resets the registers except the shadowed CLKM_CTRL.

Reached from PREP_DEEP_SLEEP (a TRX_CMD) by raising SLP_TR; everything except the SLP_TR monitor is off and the current is leakage only. Registers, AES and frame buffer are lost, the input pulls (except SLP_TR) return, and on wake-up the part comes back to TRX_OFF with CLKM at the default 1 MHz.

/RST low for at least 625 ns resets the registers and takes the chip to TRX_OFF (in 26 µs) from any state but P_ON, where it stays in P_ON. The SPI is used no sooner than 625 ns after /RST rises. A reset discards a queued SPI command. CLKM_CTRL is shadowed: the clock rate is kept but the register reads back 1, so the host rewrites it or the rate falls to 1 MHz after the next sleep.

The SPI is a slave in mode 0, MSB first, with each byte exchanged both ways. Every transfer begins with a command byte: register access (64 registers, two bytes), frame buffer access (PHR, PSDU, then LQI, ED and RX_STATUS on reads), or SRAM access from a given address (frame buffer 0x00 to 0x7F, AES 0x82 to 0x94). The first byte back can be set to show TRX_STATUS, PHY_RSSI or IRQ_STATUS. MISO is driven only while /SEL is low and has no pull-up when released. SCLK may be 8 MHz when it is derived from CLKM and 7.5 MHz otherwise.

Eight interrupt flags (nine events) are ORed onto IRQ. IRQ_MASK enables them; reading IRQ_STATUS clears all flags and the pin. Flags stay set after the cause goes away, except PLL_LOCK and PLL_UNLOCK, which clear each other. IRQ_MASK_MODE lets masked causes still show in IRQ_STATUS. IRQ is active high by default; IRQ_POLARITY inverts it.

A 16 MHz amplitude-controlled oscillator; it settles in about 180 µs after SLEEP and 330 µs after DEEP_SLEEP. The crystal's load capacitance is made up of CX, the internal trim CTRIM and the strays; the trim can only lower the frequency. A higher load capacitance makes the crystal less sensitive to strays but slows start-up and raises current. An external 16 MHz reference of 400 mV to 1 V peak-to-peak can drive XTAL1 with XTAL2 left open and XTAL_MODE set to 0x5.

CLKM gives the 16 MHz reference divided to 16, 8, 4, 2 or 1 MHz, 250 kHz or 62.5 kHz. With CLKM_SHA_SEL = 0 a new rate applies at once, glitch-free; with it set, the change waits until the next wake from SLEEP. Turning CLKM off when unused saves current and spurious emissions.

The fractional-N synthesizer covers the sixteen 5 MHz-spaced 802.15.4 channels and a 500 kHz grid from 2322 MHz to 2527 MHz. It locks in about 80 µs from TRX_OFF and changes channel in about 11 µs. In PLL_ON and receive the PLL runs 2 MHz below the transmit frequency and steps up within 16 µs before transmitting, and back within 32 µs, without lock interrupts. Centre-frequency and delay-cell calibrations run on every enable and frequency change; they can be started by hand in PLL_ON, which is advised after more than about five minutes on one channel or a large temperature change.

Output power is set by TX_PWR in 16 steps from +4 dBm to -17 dBm. A transmission starts from PLL_ON or TX_ARET_ON on a rising SLP_TR edge or the TX_START command; the PA buffer and PA ramp up in turn and modulation begins 16 µs after the trigger.

RX_PDT_LEVEL raises the level a frame must have to start the demodulator, in 3 dB steps; any non-zero setting also drops RX_ON current to 11.3 mA. RX_PDT_DIS blocks new frames while leaving the receiver on. RX_SAFE_MODE protects a received frame with a good FCS from being overwritten until the host has read it.

RSSI is a 5-bit value in 3 dB steps, updated every 2 µs while receiving. Energy detection averages RSSI over eight symbols (128 µs) into 1 dB steps, 0x00 to 0x53; it runs by hand on a write to PHY_ED_LEVEL or by itself on each SHR. CCA works in the four 802.15.4 modes with an energy threshold set by CCA_ED_THRES; a manual CCA result arrives within 180 µs and is best taken in RX_ON.

BATMON compares EVDD with a programmable threshold, 1.70 V to 2.45 V in 50 mV steps or 2.550 V to 3.675 V in 75 mV steps. BATMON_OK shows the present result and IRQ_7 fires when it falls from 1 to 0. It is inactive in P_ON, SLEEP and DEEP_SLEEP.

A hardware MAC for 802.15.4-2003/2006/2011 frames. RX_AACK receives, checks the FCS and address fields, flags an address match and sends the acknowledgement by itself, including slotted ACK timed by SLP_TR. TX_ARET runs CSMA-CA with random backoff and CCA retries, sends with an automatic FCS, waits for the ACK and retries when it does not come, then reports the result in TRAC_STATUS.

A stand-alone 128-bit AES engine is reached through the SRAM access mode and works in every state except SLEEP and DEEP_SLEEP, alongside radio activity; one AES core cycle takes about 24 µs. A two-bit noise-based random value in PHY_RSSI updates every 1 µs in the basic receive states, for CSMA seeds and keys; it needs the preamble detector enabled.

OQPSK_DATA_RATE selects 500, 1000 or 2000 kb/s for the PSDU in the same channel bandwidth; the header stays at 250 kb/s and sensitivity drops with the spreading. Nothing in the header signals the rate, so both ends are set alike in advance, or a non-standard SFD marks it. The -ZF parts support 250 kb/s only.

With ANT_EXT_SW_EN set, DIG1 and DIG2 drive an external antenna switch. With ANT_DIV_EN set the chip searches both antennas for a valid frame, locks on one and reports it in ANT_SEL; an RX_AACK acknowledgement goes out on the same antenna and TX_ARET alternates antennas on retries. ANT_CTRL fixes one antenna instead. PDT_THRES is set to 3 while diversity is on. Disable the switch outputs outside receive and transmit to save current.

With PA_EXT_EN set, DIG3 goes high and DIG4 low while transmitting, the opposite otherwise, to steer an external PA, LNA and switches. The pins change 6 µs after the transmit request and switch back 3 µs after the internal PA turns off. Disabled, both are pulled to analog ground; disable them outside receive and transmit to save current.

Register 0x16 enables several self-running savings: PLL energy saving cuts PLL_ON current from 5.2 mA to 450 µA; smart receiving cuts average RX_ON current by up to half; extended desensitizing lowers RX current further with RX_PDT_LEVEL (0x08 gives -83 dBm sensitivity at much lower current); automatic ACK power lowers ACK output power for strong, high-LQI links down to -17 dBm; PAN address match stops listening early on a foreign PAN. 0xFF enables all of them and 0xC1 or 0x01 turns them off.

All digital outputs and CLKM have a fixed drive and are meant for at most 50 pF. The inputs have pulls only in P_ON and DEEP_SLEEP; in every other state the host keeps them at a defined level, since floating inputs can raise sleep current.

Rarely, PLL_LOCK does not arrive within the 250 µs maximum. The remedy: read PLL_CF, invert its least significant bit, write it back with the upper four bits unchanged, and wait about 80 µs more or for the interrupt.
Reflow follows IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020C.
